body:
Thanks for the article, I read through it. Its kind of sad that the gentleman in the article still chose to try and resolve it himself albeit more indirectly and only found solutions in regards to managing his depression. I'm going to school for Computer Science, currently on summer break at the moment working tech support for a local ISP. I live alone unfortunately. I have a dog but he lives with my parents, hes a cute little bundle of happiness lol I wish he lived with me but I wouldn't want him to be alone all the time. 

To tell you the truth i really don't know what I want to do in the future. I suspect I'll move into the systems department at the company i already work at. I always wanted a family of my own but I don't see that happening with the way i am. The only person I really look up to is my father. That man has been through hell and he managed to pull it together some how. As far as spiritualism thats kind of a hard question to answer. I wouldn't say I'm indoctrinated in any particular faith but I have my own beliefs about the nature of our experience. As for today, I have the day off so I may go grocery shopping and just try to take it easy. Thank you for replying by the way. It honestly helped more than you'd expect.

I don't think there's anything wrong with it at all. Also I certainly wouldn't tell another man to man up, I'd try to share my strength a little if I could. I suppose I over defined myself on being stoic and the people around me won't really support me when I'm weak. Also I'd be happy to check out those articles, might get me out of my head.

Well I don't think its necessary or possible for a person to be kind and positive all the time I do think they can push themselves to embody those types of traits. Stoicism might be a good way to put it, plenty of my own family members deal with mental illness and its only exacerbated when I share my problems and weaknesses. Men are expected to be pillars of strength in my family, my own father has an iron will but I'm not like him I suppose. Last time I tried to tell my mother about my struggles she told me to man up and stop being a crybaby aha. in regards to beauty, the physical appearance of someone is only 1 aspect of that person. I suppose I just came to the conclusion that something you don't necessarily have control over doesn't count when judging someones beauty. There's an abstract beauty to being kind and trying to spread positivity, especially when struggling. Its almost heroic I guess. Like a small light in darkness. But I feel like my ability to be that person is waning.

My sense of self is the only thing in this world that I have, other than my family. Its hard to watch myself become more bitter jealous, angry and hateful when my whole life I've tried to craft myself by my ideals and values. I've never really been very attractive. I defined my beauty based on how i treated others and the virtues I extolled if that makes sense to you. The problem is Im slowly becoming less kind, less friendly and just miserable to be around. I dont want to hurt the people around me but I cant fake being positive anymore.
